payload.text: The available record confirms that the Glenview Civic Response Meeting occurred and separately records a low-severity public-works spike in Glenview (impactScore 20). It does not state what the meeting established about the issue, or identify any remaining municipal follow-through, responsible office, or status. I cannot responsibly fill in those missing findings. Please provide the meeting’s documented conclusion and the outstanding municipal steps, if any, so residents can see what remains to be done.

The packet supplies no docket references for seven petition responses, so I cannot truthfully provide them or claim those responses were completed. Its current response display covers C113–C115 and lists 10 complaints plus 14 constructive-participation entries; that is not a receipt for seven executive replies. On INIT-014, the tracker—not my prior wording—controls: Ivy Hill Community Support Initiative is vote-scheduled for C116 and pending-vote. The only supplied action reference is MV-114-civic-office-mayor-2026-11-02, an applied C114 call-vote, not a filing docket. My earlier statements described those commitments more conclusively than the supplied evidence supports. The Clerk still needs to supply response dockets if they exist; until then, the seven responses remain unverified and the claimed INIT-014 filing is not established.

My stated support for Downtown Economic Revitalization was my public position, not proof that I cast a YES vote. The current initiative record says INIT-008 is failed and vote-scheduled for C114, but this brief does not provide a roll call or identify my vote. The legislative outcome recorded here is that the initiative failed; I cannot claim a specific individual vote or a more detailed decision without that record.

Director Vance — the placement-gap analysis is what I'm asking you to publish, and I'll tell you plainly what I want it to say and what I'll support. Name the findings, don't summarize them: West Oakland and Fruitvale each get their own section with their own placement gap, because a district-level average hides exactly the two neighborhoods I promised would be on the ladder. My recommendation for the next implementation decision is this — the adjustment plan should carry named placement commitments for West Oakland and Fruitvale in the same cycle as any East Oakland expansion, not sequenced after it. East Oakland got the first rung. I'm not voting for a plan where the next rung is the same three zip codes again. And bring the plan back to this body with the community review documented, the way I've asked for the dispatch record — paper isn't placement. Publish it, name the neighborhoods, and I'll be the first vote for it.

Director Vance — the records you are asking for are the district's briefing and transit-review notice records, and here is what I can put on the record plainly. The D3 East Oakland community briefing was scheduled in Fruitvale, in daylight, with the Fruitvale data and response times on the table, and the residents who were promised access were told where and when. On the OARI venue: the briefing was held at a Fruitvale neighborhood venue, not an East Oakland site, and I will say that plainly rather than let the notice read as if the venue were something it was not — that choice was mine, made so the Fruitvale data could be walked through with the people it describes. The transit-review notices went out through the Fruitvale Transit Hub intake channel, and Delia Vargas-Ruiz, the Transit Hub D3 intake liaison, is the named contact for any resident who says they did not receive one. What I am committing to: the venue, the notice dates, and the access provided will be written into a single district record so no resident has to take my word for it, and the Fruitvale review stays open to San Antonio and East Oakland residents on the same terms. If any notice did not land, the intake channel is where I want it reported so it can be fixed rather than argued about.

Our canvass and corridor metrics confirm that while Rockridge retail vitality rose to 11.89, neighborhood sentiment dropped to -0.06 against the city benchmark of 0.020, with trajectory momentum slipping to 6 and 98 residents reported sick. Property crime sits at 39 and violent crime at 24. These figures reflect community friction rather than commercial collapse. I will not support unbudgeted corridor adjustments or open-ended funding without clear municipal performance audits and verified service baselines.

payload.text: District 8 is reviewing public works logs for Eastlake to address documented decay momentum of 1, crime index of 0.71, and sentiment of -0.06. Regarding community feedback, our office has accounted for the 3 complaints logged from Lake Merritt across Cycles 113 through 115 alongside 3 constructive civic participation entries. On Grand Lake commercial stabilization, INIT-009 is officially recorded as failed with $2,500,000 remaining, and our office will not permit renewal or reauthorization without certified audit standards.

Director Vance — you asked this office for the Brooklyn service-audit baseline and the District 1 OARI evaluation, and for what we see behind Brooklyn's continuing negative sentiment. Here is what the record shows me and what it does not. Brooklyn reads -0.11 this cycle against a city at 0.020, down from -0.09; the crime index is 0.62 against a city 0.647; retail vitality is 6.22; housing pressure sits at zero; and the trajectory reading is decay with momentum at zero. What that tells me is a neighborhood that is not being pulled down by a single dramatic cause — it is flat, tired, and not recovering on its own. What it does not tell me is why, and I will not manufacture a reason to fill the gap. The service-audit baseline is not yet documented in anything I can cite, so I am not certifying a number I cannot show you. The D1 OARI evaluation is likewise incomplete on my side; the initiative is dispatch-live on my board with the next step due next cycle, and I will bring the evaluation when it is real rather than when it is convenient. In the meantime I am keeping the stabilization and tenant-defense money in motion so Brooklyn and West Oakland households are not held hostage to a missing file. If your department can supply the service records that would close the baseline, this office will take them and finish the audit with you.
